q: Am I eligible for PMAY 2.0 in 2026?
a: You are eligible if your family meets ALL six conditions: (1) annual household income up to Rs 9 lakh (EWS up to Rs 3L, LIG Rs 3-6L, MIG Rs 6-9L); (2) you or any family member do not own a pucca house anywhere in India; (3) the family has not been a beneficiary of any central, state or local government housing scheme in the last 20 years; (4) the property is priced at Rs 35 lakh or less; (5) the home loan amount is Rs 25 lakh or less (subsidy is on the first Rs 8 lakh only); (6) carpet area is up to 120 square metres. Additionally, for EWS and LIG categories female ownership is mandatory - the property must be in the name of a female family member, jointly or solely. For MIG category female ownership is NOT mandatory. Scheme is active from September 2024 to August 2029 - only loans sanctioned and disbursed in this window qualify.
source_title: PMAY 2.0 Eligibility Checker — Will You Get the ₹1.80L Subsidy?

q: How much PMAY subsidy will I actually get?
a: The maximum subsidy under PMAY-U 2.0 ISS is Rs 1.80 lakh per family, paid out in 5 equal annual instalments of Rs 36,000 each. The NPV (Net Present Value, discounted at 8.5%) is capped at Rs 1.50 lakh. The subsidy is credited directly to your home loan account by the lender (PLI). Mechanically, the subsidy reduces your outstanding principal by approximately Rs 1.50 lakh upfront (the NPV value), and your EMI is recalculated on the reduced principal at the bank's regular interest rate. For a Rs 15 lakh loan at 8 percent for 20 years, this typically saves Rs 1,100-1,200 per month in EMI. The smaller your loan and the longer your tenure beyond 12 years, the smaller the relative benefit - the sweet spot is loans of about Rs 8-15 lakh with 12-year tenure.
source_title: PMAY 2.0 Eligibility Checker — Will You Get the ₹1.80L Subsidy?

q: What documents are needed for PMAY 2.0?
a: For the PMAY-U 2.0 application you will need: Aadhaar card and PAN card of all family members (mandatory for DBT linkage); income proof - Form 16, latest 3 months' salary slips for salaried, or 2 years' ITR for self-employed; bank statement (last 6 months); address proof (Voter ID, Aadhaar, utility bill or ration card); property documents (sale agreement or builder allotment letter); self-declaration that you do not own a pucca house anywhere in India and have not been a prior PMAY beneficiary; for EWS/LIG, a self-attested income certificate (income certificate from a Tehsildar or equivalent is preferred but self-attestation is allowed for the Rs 9 lakh and below segments). The lender (PLI) handles the subsidy claim through the Unified Web Portal within 30 days of loan disbursement - you do not need to submit a separate subsidy application to MoHUA.
source_title: PMAY 2.0 Eligibility Checker — Will You Get the ₹1.80L Subsidy?

q: Why is female ownership mandatory for EWS and LIG?
a: Female ownership is mandatory for EWS (income up to Rs 3 lakh) and LIG (income Rs 3-6 lakh) categories under PMAY-U 2.0 as a social policy mandate - the scheme aims to empower women in lower-income households through asset ownership. The property must be registered in the name of a female family member, either as sole owner or jointly with the male earner. This requirement reflects evidence that female asset ownership in low-income households reduces domestic violence risk, improves child education outcomes, and stabilises household finances. For the MIG category (income Rs 6-9 lakh) female ownership is NOT mandatory - the legislature judged that this higher-income segment has less urgent need for the gender-protective measure. If you fall in EWS/LIG and the only earner in the family is male, you can still qualify - just register the property jointly in his and his spouse's or mother's name.
source_title: PMAY 2.0 Eligibility Checker — Will You Get the ₹1.80L Subsidy?

q: Can I claim PMAY 2.0 if I already have a home loan?
a: Only if your home loan was sanctioned AND disbursed on or after 1 September 2024 - this is the absolute cutoff. Loans sanctioned before this date are governed by the prior PMAY 1.0 / CLSS scheme, which closed for new applications on 31 March 2022. If your current loan is from before September 2024 you cannot claim PMAY 2.0 ISS on it directly. Two workarounds in some cases: (a) if you transfer your existing loan to a new lender after 1 September 2024, the new loan technically counts as a fresh disbursement and may be eligible - check with the new PLI; (b) if you take a top-up loan on or after 1 September 2024 from your current lender for an eligible purpose (purchase, construction, enhancement), that top-up portion may qualify. Both routes are subject to the PLI's interpretation and the unified web portal's validation - confirm before banking on it.
source_title: PMAY 2.0 Eligibility Checker — Will You Get the ₹1.80L Subsidy?

q: How is LTCG calculated on property sale after Budget 2024?
a: From 23 July 2024 onwards, the Finance Act 2024 changed the LTCG regime for immovable property. For properties ACQUIRED BEFORE 23 July 2024 and sold thereafter, you have a CHOICE: pay 12.5 percent tax without indexation, OR 20 percent tax with indexation, whichever is lower. For properties ACQUIRED ON OR AFTER 23 July 2024, only the 12.5 percent without indexation rate applies. The 24-month holding-period threshold for LTCG on immovable property is unchanged. Indexation uses the Cost Inflation Index notified by CBDT; for FY 2025-26 the CII is 376 (base year FY 2001-02 = 100). For older properties with high inflation between purchase and sale, the 20 percent with indexation option usually wins by a wide margin. For recently purchased properties, the 12.5 percent without indexation option usually wins.
source_title: LTCG on Property Sale — 12.5% or 20%? The Calculator Picks for You

q: What is Section 54 exemption on LTCG from property sale?
a: Section 54 of the Income Tax Act gives an LTCG exemption when you sell a long-term residential house property and reinvest the capital gain (not the full sale value, just the gain) into another residential house in India. The new house must be purchased within 1 year before or 2 years after the sale date, OR constructed within 3 years. The exemption equals the lower of: (a) the actual LTCG, or (b) the amount invested in the new house. The new property is locked in for 3 years - selling it earlier reverses the exemption. Budget 2023 capped the maximum exemption under Section 54 at Rs 10 crore per assessee. If you don't immediately reinvest, you can park the gain in a Capital Gains Account Scheme (CGAS) at any nationalised bank before the ITR filing due date, and use it for the new house within the time limit.
source_title: LTCG on Property Sale — 12.5% or 20%? The Calculator Picks for You

q: How is Section 54F different from Section 54?
a: Section 54 applies when you sell a residential house and reinvest into another residential house. Section 54F applies when you sell ANY OTHER long-term capital asset (a plot of land, commercial property, gold, shares) and reinvest into a residential house. The biggest difference: Section 54F requires reinvesting the entire NET SALE CONSIDERATION (not just the gain) for full exemption - and gives pro-rata exemption if you invest less. Section 54 only requires reinvesting the gain. Section 54F has an additional condition: you must not own more than one residential house at the time of the original sale (apart from the one being purchased). Both sections have the same time limits (1 year before/2 years after for purchase, 3 years for construction) and the same Rs 10 crore Budget 2023 cap.
source_title: LTCG on Property Sale — 12.5% or 20%? The Calculator Picks for You

q: What is the Rs 50 lakh limit under Section 54EC?
a: Section 54EC allows you to invest your LTCG from sale of land or building into specified bonds (NHAI, REC, PFC, IRFC - the 'capital gain bonds') and claim exemption. The investment must be made within 6 months of the sale date. The maximum exemption is capped at Rs 50 lakh per financial year. Because of the 6-month window, you can split a sale across two financial years to claim Rs 50 lakh in each year, but only if the sale date and the 6-month window straddle a 31 March boundary - in practice, total exemption is capped at Rs 50 lakh for most sales. The bonds have a 5-year lock-in (was 3 years before 2018) and pay around 5.25 percent annual interest. This option is most useful when your LTCG is between Rs 1 lakh and Rs 50 lakh and you don't want to commit to a new property purchase.
source_title: LTCG on Property Sale — 12.5% or 20%? The Calculator Picks for You

q: Can I combine Section 54, 54F, and 54EC exemptions on the same sale?
a: Yes, exemptions are stackable when applied to different parts of the LTCG amount. For example, if you sell a residential house and have an LTCG of Rs 1 crore, you could: invest Rs 50 lakh in Section 54EC bonds (full exemption under 54EC), and use the remaining Rs 50 lakh gain to purchase another residential house (full exemption under Section 54). Total exemption: Rs 1 crore, tax payable: zero. However, you cannot claim the SAME amount under two sections - no double-dipping. For Section 54 vs 54F, you cannot use both for the same sale because they apply to different originating asset types (residential vs other). The combined exemption cap is the Rs 10 crore ceiling under each of 54 and 54F (Budget 2023 cap) plus Rs 50 lakh under 54EC.
source_title: LTCG on Property Sale — 12.5% or 20%? The Calculator Picks for You

q: How much does waterproofing cost in India 2026?
a: Waterproofing in India costs ₹40–500 per sqft depending on method. Cementitious coating (basic) is ₹40–80/sqft with 5–7 year life. Acrylic coating (Dr Fixit Roofseal) is ₹70–120/sqft, 5–8 year life. APP membrane (the terrace standard) is ₹140–260/sqft with 10–15 year life. PU coating ₹120–220/sqft, EPDM sheet ₹220–380/sqft (15–20 year life), and PMMA ₹280–500/sqft. For an 800 sqft terrace, expect ₹50,000 (cementitious) to ₹3 lakh (APP membrane on existing leaking surface) to ₹5 lakh (premium EPDM sheet).
source_title: Waterproofing Cost Calculator — India 2026

q: What is the best waterproofing method for terrace in India?
a: For a typical Indian residential terrace, APP/SBS torch-applied membrane is the standard recommendation — ₹140–260/sqft with 10–15 year life. It handles thermal expansion, monsoon, and direct sunlight well. Acrylic coating (₹70–120/sqft) is acceptable for low-budget new construction but needs reapplication every 5–7 years. EPDM rubber sheet (₹220–380/sqft) is the premium choice for villa terraces with 15–20 year life. Avoid cementitious-only on terraces — it cracks under thermal cycling within 3–4 years and triggers leaks.
source_title: Waterproofing Cost Calculator — India 2026

q: How long does waterproofing last in India?
a: Waterproofing lifespan in Indian conditions: cementitious 5–7 years, acrylic 5–8 years, PU 8–12 years, APP membrane 10–15 years, EPDM 15–20 years, PMMA 15+ years. Actual life depends heavily on application quality, surface preparation, and whether water ponds on the surface (poor slope reduces life by 40–60%). Manufacturer warranty is typically 5 years, but real-world life varies by ±30% based on contractor quality. The biggest single factor is screed slope correction — if water ponds, even ₹500/sqft PMMA fails in 5 years.
source_title: Waterproofing Cost Calculator — India 2026

q: Should I waterproof my terrace before or after a leak?
a: Always before. Preventive terrace waterproofing during construction or as part of a planned maintenance cycle costs 30–50% less than reactive leak repair. Once a leak starts, you typically need crack injection (₹35–70/sqft of crack area), screed replacement if water has caused efflorescence (₹80–150/sqft), and the actual waterproofing layer on top — totaling 1.4–1.8× the preventive cost. Plus the interior repair (peeling paint, stained ceiling, damaged electricals) adds ₹15,000–60,000 for an average bedroom. Cheapest waterproofing is the one done before a leak.
source_title: Waterproofing Cost Calculator — India 2026

q: Is Dr Fixit waterproofing reliable?
a: Dr Fixit (Pidilite) is a leading consumer-grade waterproofing brand in India and reliable when applied per manufacturer guidelines. Their range covers cementitious slurry (Pidiproof LW+), acrylic coating (Roofseal), and bathroom waterproofing (Bathseal). Real-world performance is similar to MYK Laticrete, Asian Paints SmartCare, Sika and Fosroc — all are reputable. The single biggest determinant of waterproofing performance is not brand choice but application quality: surface preparation, primer use, and number of coats. A poor contractor with Dr Fixit will leak; a skilled contractor with a generic acrylic will hold.
source_title: Waterproofing Cost Calculator — India 2026

q: How do I know if my contractor's rate per sqft is fair?
a: Compare the quoted rate to current market benchmarks for your city and quality grade. Economy construction in metros should cost ₹1,400–1,600/sqft, standard ₹1,900–2,100/sqft, premium ₹2,800–3,200/sqft. If the quote is more than 20% above these ranges, ask for an itemised breakdown and get at least one more quote.
source_title: Contractor Quote Checker — Is Your Rate Fair?

q: What is a reasonable markup for a contractor on materials?
a: A reasonable contractor markup on materials is 10–15%. Anything above 20% is excessive. Ask your contractor for material invoices, or better yet, buy key materials (cement, steel, tiles) directly from dealers and only pay the contractor for labour.
source_title: Contractor Quote Checker — Is Your Rate Fair?

q: Should I be suspicious of very low contractor quotes?
a: Yes. Unusually low quotes (more than 20–25% below market rates) almost always indicate either very low-quality materials, scope exclusions that will be added later as 'extras', or contractors who'll ask for large advance payments and disappear. Always verify what's included in a low quote item by item.
source_title: Contractor Quote Checker — Is Your Rate Fair?

q: What payment structure should I insist on with a contractor?
a: The safest payment structure is: 30% on contract signing, 30% when the structure (slab/columns) is complete, 30% when finishing begins, and the final 10% only after snag-free handover. Never pay more than 30% upfront. Avoid contractors who demand 50%+ advance.
source_title: Contractor Quote Checker — Is Your Rate Fair?

q: What documents should I get from a contractor before starting?
a: Insist on: a written, itemised quote with material specifications (grades, brands), a project timeline with milestones, a formal agreement with payment schedule and penalty clauses for delays, and the contractor's GST number and Aadhaar/PAN. Check references from 2–3 previous clients specifically.
source_title: Contractor Quote Checker — Is Your Rate Fair?

q: Why is comparing monthly EMI to monthly rent the wrong way to decide?
a: It ignores three big factors. First, the opportunity cost of your down payment — if you didn't lock that money in property, it could be earning 10–12% in equity mutual funds. Second, rent escalation — your rent will roughly double in 12 years at 6% annual escalation. Third, property appreciation — your property's value also compounds. A proper rent vs buy decision requires simulating wealth year-by-year in both scenarios with the same monthly cash budget. That's what this calculator does.
source_title: EMI vs Rent — Should You Buy or Keep Renting?

q: What is the break-even year and how is it calculated?
a: The break-even year is the year at which your net wealth in the BUY scenario (property equity = property value minus remaining loan balance) first equals or exceeds your net wealth in the RENT scenario (compounded value of your invested down payment plus the monthly EMI-vs-rent differential). Before that year, renting and investing wins; after that year, buying wins. The calculator computes this month-by-month and reports the first year buying overtakes.
source_title: EMI vs Rent — Should You Buy or Keep Renting?

q: What property appreciation rate should I assume for India?
a: For Tier-1 cities (Mumbai, Bangalore, Delhi NCR, Pune, Hyderabad, Chennai), assume 5–8% annual appreciation in established neighbourhoods over a 7-year+ horizon. Peripheral and Outer Ring Road corridors have outpaced 8–10% in many cases. Tier-2 cities range 4–7%. Cap the assumption at 8% for a base-case scenario; anything above 10% is optimistic and the deal becomes very sensitive to that assumption. The calculator lets you stress-test by changing the appreciation rate.
source_title: EMI vs Rent — Should You Buy or Keep Renting?

q: Should I include rental yield in the buying scenario?
a: This calculator assumes you live in the property if you buy — so no rental income. If you intend to buy and rent it out (i.e. it's an investment property, not a primary residence), the analysis changes: you would add 2.5–3.5% gross rental yield (typical Indian metro yields) minus 30–35% costs (vacancy, repairs, society dues, taxes) to the BUY scenario's wealth growth. For a primary-residence decision, the calculator's current setup is correct.
source_title: EMI vs Rent — Should You Buy or Keep Renting?

q: What is a realistic alternative investment return to assume?
a: For a 7–15 year horizon: equity mutual funds (Nifty 50 / Sensex SIP) have delivered 11–13% CAGR over rolling 10-year windows. Hybrid funds: 9–10%. Pure debt or FD: 7–7.5%. Use 10–11% if you would actually invest in equity, 7–8% if you're risk-averse. The calculator's verdict is sensitive to this — try both endpoints to see how much your assumption matters.
source_title: EMI vs Rent — Should You Buy or Keep Renting?

q: What is the average construction cost per sqft in India in 2026?
a: In 2026, construction cost per sqft in India ranges from ₹850 (Economy, Tier-3 cities) to ₹2,800 (Premium, Metro cities). Standard quality construction in a metro city typically costs around ₹1,900 per sqft.
source_title: Home Construction Cost Calculator India 2026

q: How is house construction cost calculated?
a: House construction cost is calculated by multiplying the built-up area (plot area × number of floors) by the construction rate per sqft. The rate varies based on city, quality grade, and materials chosen.
source_title: Home Construction Cost Calculator India 2026

q: Does construction cost include interior work?
a: Typically, the basic construction cost covers structural work, basic flooring, plastering, and standard electrical and plumbing. Premium interior finishes like modular kitchens, false ceilings, and designer tiles are usually separate.
source_title: Home Construction Cost Calculator India 2026

q: Why should I add a contingency amount to my construction budget?
a: Construction projects almost always encounter unexpected costs — soil issues, material price increases, design changes, or weather delays. A 10–15% contingency buffer ensures your project isn't stalled by surprise expenses.
source_title: Home Construction Cost Calculator India 2026

q: How can I reduce my house construction cost?
a: Key savings strategies include: getting at least 3 contractor quotes, buying materials directly from dealers (not through the contractor), building in stages, choosing a simple floor plan, and locking material prices in advance.
source_title: Home Construction Cost Calculator India 2026

q: What is the difference between Economy, Standard, and Premium construction?
a: Economy uses basic materials like local bricks, standard cement, basic tiles and simple electrical fittings. Standard uses branded materials, good quality tiles, modular switches and better finishes. Premium uses high-end materials, designer tiles, imported fittings and superior finishing throughout.

q: What is stamp duty on property in India?
a: Stamp duty is a tax paid to the state government when you register a property purchase. It varies between 3% and 8% of the property value depending on the state, the buyer's gender (most states give a 1–2% concession to female buyers), the city (rural vs urban), and the property type (residential vs commercial). Registration fee is a separate 1%.
source_title: Stamp Duty & Registration Calculator — India 2026

q: Do women pay less stamp duty in India?
a: Yes, in most states women receive a 1–2% concession on stamp duty when the property is registered solely in their name. Maharashtra, Delhi, Punjab, Haryana, Rajasthan, and UP all offer such concessions. For joint registration (husband + wife), most states apply the female rate. Always verify the current concession at your state IGR website.
source_title: Stamp Duty & Registration Calculator — India 2026

q: Is stamp duty same for under-construction and ready-to-move properties?
a: Stamp duty rates are the same. However, under-construction properties also attract 5% GST (1% for affordable housing) on the property value, which is a separate tax. Ready-to-move properties with completion certificate are GST-exempt, making them ~5% cheaper overall on tax burden.
source_title: Stamp Duty & Registration Calculator — India 2026

q: Can stamp duty be paid in installments?
a: No. Stamp duty must be paid in full before registration. It cannot be financed separately by the bank, but most home loans factor stamp duty into the total project cost (typically up to 90% of property value plus stamp duty).
source_title: Stamp Duty & Registration Calculator — India 2026

q: Is stamp duty refundable if the deal falls through?
a: Stamp duty is partially refundable (typically 90–95% of paid amount) if you apply within 6 months of purchase and the document was not registered. After registration, refund is much harder and limited to specific cases like cancelled allotments. Each state has its own refund process via the IGR office.
source_title: Stamp Duty & Registration Calculator — India 2026

q: How many contractor quotes should I get before building?
a: Get at least 3 quotes from different contractors. Studies of Indian residential construction show that the spread between the lowest and highest quote for identical specifications is typically 15–30%. Getting 3 quotes gives you enough range to identify the market rate and negotiate confidently.
source_title: How to Get & Compare Contractor Quotes in India — The Right Way

q: What should a contractor quote include?
a: A proper contractor quote should include: built-up area in sqft, specification of materials (cement brand, steel grade, brick type), labour rates, payment schedule tied to milestones, timeline with start and completion dates, what is excluded (electrification, plumbing, finishing), and a 10–15% contingency line. Any quote missing these items cannot be fairly compared.
source_title: How to Get & Compare Contractor Quotes in India — The Right Way

q: How do I find a good contractor for house construction in India?
a: The most reliable method is referrals from people who recently built — not online directories. Ask your architect or structural engineer (they work with contractors regularly). Check with your local building material dealers (they know which contractors buy quality materials). Visit 1–2 completed projects of any contractor before signing.
source_title: How to Get & Compare Contractor Quotes in India — The Right Way

q: What are red flags in a contractor quote?
a: Red flags: quote significantly lower than two others (will cut corners or add costs later), no payment schedule (demands large upfront advance), no material specifications listed, refuses to sign a written agreement, asks for more than 10% advance before work starts, cannot provide references from recent projects.
source_title: How to Get & Compare Contractor Quotes in India — The Right Way

q: How much advance should I pay a contractor?
a: Never pay more than 10% of project value upfront. A legitimate contractor with good cash flow does not need a large advance. Tie all payments to construction milestones: foundation complete, slab cast, walls up, roof done, finishing complete. Final 10% paid only after your independent inspection confirms all work is satisfactory.
source_title: How to Get & Compare Contractor Quotes in India — The Right Way

q: Is it better to hire a contractor on labour-only or turnkey basis?
a: Labour-only (you buy materials) gives you 15–25% savings but requires time to manage material procurement. Turnkey (contractor supplies everything) is more convenient but carries higher markup risk. For most owner-builders, a hybrid approach works best: turnkey for civil structure (foundation to roof), labour-only for finishing (tiles, paint, fixtures) where material quality matters most and markups are highest.
source_title: How to Get & Compare Contractor Quotes in India — The Right Way

q: How much does a modular kitchen cost in India 2026?
a: Q2 2026 modular kitchen rates per running foot (rft), inclusive of base+wall unit carcass, shutters and standard Indian hardware: Laminate finish ₹9,500–14,000/rft, Membrane (PVC) ₹11,000–15,500/rft, Acrylic high-gloss ₹15,000–22,000/rft, PU (polyurethane) ₹18,000–28,000/rft, Lacquered glass ₹22,000–32,000/rft. A standard 12 rft L-shape kitchen with laminate finish, granite countertop, mid-range hardware and basic chimney+hob ranges ₹1.6–2.5 lakh in metros. Premium PU or acrylic finish in the same layout: ₹3.4–5.2 lakh.
source_title: Modular Kitchen Cost Calculator — ₹9,500–32,000/rft, Real Q2 2026 Rates

q: Branded showroom vs local carpenter — what is the actual price difference?
a: Branded showrooms (Sleek, Hettich Studio, Hafele Aspekt, Godrej Interio, IKEA, Livspace) typically cost 30–60% more than a skilled local carpenter quoting the same materials. The branded premium pays for: design software (3D mockups), warranty (5–10 years on hardware), assured material quality, faster delivery, and showroom overheads. A local carpenter using Greenply BWP plywood and Hettich hardware can deliver near-equivalent quality at ₹12,000–18,000/rft for laminate; the same setup at a branded showroom is ₹18,000–28,000/rft. The risk with the carpenter route is material substitution and no enforceable warranty.
source_title: Modular Kitchen Cost Calculator — ₹9,500–32,000/rft, Real Q2 2026 Rates

q: Acrylic vs PU vs laminate finish — which is best for Indian kitchens?
a: Laminate is the most practical for India: ₹9,500–14,000/rft, easy to clean, durable for 10–12 years, repairable. Acrylic is high-gloss and looks premium but scratches show easily and yellowing happens after 5–7 years in heavy-cooking households. PU (polyurethane) is the best premium option: scratch-resistant, can be re-sprayed in 8–10 years for refresh, but ₹18,000–28,000/rft. For most Indian kitchens with daily heavy cooking (oil splatter, high humidity), laminate or PU is the practical choice. Skip acrylic if your cooking is heavy-tadka style.
source_title: Modular Kitchen Cost Calculator — ₹9,500–32,000/rft, Real Q2 2026 Rates

q: What is the cost difference between L-shape and U-shape kitchen?
a: For the same finish and hardware, U-shape costs roughly 35–60% more than L-shape because of the extra running feet (typical L-shape 12–16 rft, U-shape 16–22 rft) and additional corner units. A standard L-shape laminate kitchen ₹1.6–2.5 lakh; equivalent U-shape ₹2.4–3.6 lakh. U-shape only makes sense if your kitchen room is at least 8x10 feet — otherwise the working triangle becomes cramped. Parallel/galley layout is similar to L-shape in cost but needs at least 7 feet of width between two runs.
source_title: Modular Kitchen Cost Calculator — ₹9,500–32,000/rft, Real Q2 2026 Rates

q: Should I get a granite or quartz countertop?
a: For Indian kitchens, granite remains the value choice: ₹150–280/sqft, indestructible against hot vessels, lasts decades. Quartz (engineered stone) at ₹400–700/sqft is uniform-looking, less porous than granite, and stain-resistant — good for kitchens where appearance matters. Avoid pure marble in kitchens (stains from turmeric, tomato, lemon). Solid surface (Corian-equivalent) at ₹600–1200/sqft offers seamless joints and curved edges but can scorch under hot pans — only get if you prioritise looks over toughness. For 90% of Indian kitchens, granite is the right answer.
source_title: Modular Kitchen Cost Calculator — ₹9,500–32,000/rft, Real Q2 2026 Rates

q: How much does interior design cost for a 2BHK in India?
a: A 2BHK interior in India costs ₹4.5–18 lakh depending on city and quality. Standard quality in metro cities (Bangalore, Mumbai) typically runs ₹7–10 lakh covering kitchen, wardrobes, living room, false ceiling, and painting.
source_title: Home Interior Cost Estimator India 2026

q: What is included in a full home interior package?
a: A full home interior package typically includes modular kitchen, bedroom wardrobes, TV unit/living room furniture, false ceiling in main areas, lighting, painting, and additional electrical points. Beds, sofas, dining tables, and curtains are usually separate furniture budgets.
source_title: Home Interior Cost Estimator India 2026

q: Is it cheaper to get a contractor or interior designer in India?
a: A local contractor is 15–25% cheaper than a full-service interior design firm. However, design firms handle procurement, project management, and quality control, which can save you time and prevent costly mistakes. For a 2BHK budget below ₹8 lakh, a good contractor works fine. Above ₹15 lakh, a designer often pays for themselves.

q: How long does full home interior work take?
a: A 2BHK full interior typically takes 45–75 days from order to handover. A 3BHK takes 60–90 days. Modular units (kitchen, wardrobes) take 21–28 days to manufacture after design approval. Factor in 2–3 weeks for painting, electrical, and final touches.
source_title: Home Interior Cost Estimator India 2026

q: What is the best plywood grade for home interiors in India?
a: BWR (Boiling Water Resistant) 18mm grade plywood is the standard recommendation for Indian homes. It handles humidity well and is ISI-certified. MR (Moisture Resistant) grade is cheaper but not suitable for kitchens or bathrooms. Commercial brands: Greenply, CenturyPly, Kitply are reliable.

q: How can I save money on my home interior?
a: Top savings: choose laminate shutters over acrylic (40–60% cheaper, negligible quality difference for most rooms), use PVC instead of gypsum for bathroom false ceilings, buy hardware (hinges, channels) directly from dealers, get 3 quotes, and skip false ceilings in bedrooms and utility areas.
source_title: Home Interior Cost Estimator India 2026

q: What is the current home loan interest rate in India 2026?
a: In May 2026, home loan interest rates from major Indian banks range from 7.10% to 9.5% per annum. After the December 2025 RBI repo cut to 5.25%, best rates dropped sharply — Bank of Baroda from 7.10%, SBI from 7.50%, HDFC from 7.75%, ICICI from 7.50% (pre-approved). Smaller banks and HFCs charge 8.0–9.5%. Rates depend on credit score, loan amount, and LTV ratio.
source_title: Home Loan EMI Calculator India 2026

q: How is EMI calculated for a home loan?
a: EMI = P × r × (1+r)^n / ((1+r)^n - 1), where P is the principal loan amount, r is the monthly interest rate (annual rate divided by 12 and 100), and n is the number of monthly installments (tenure in years × 12).
source_title: Home Loan EMI Calculator India 2026

q: Should I choose a shorter or longer loan tenure?
a: A shorter tenure means higher EMI but much lower total interest paid. A longer tenure lowers your monthly burden but you pay significantly more interest over the loan's life. For example, a ₹50 lakh loan at 8.0% for 20 years has an EMI of ₹41,822 and total interest of ₹50.4 lakh. The same loan for 10 years has EMI of ₹60,663 but total interest of only ₹22.8 lakh.
source_title: Home Loan EMI Calculator India 2026

q: What is prepayment and how does it help?
a: Prepayment means paying extra amounts toward your loan principal, either as a lump sum or by increasing your monthly EMI. Even one extra EMI per year can reduce your loan tenure by 2–3 years and save lakhs in interest. Most banks allow prepayment on floating-rate home loans without penalty.
source_title: Home Loan EMI Calculator India 2026

q: What is the maximum home loan I can get in India?
a: Banks typically lend up to 75–90% of the property value (LTV ratio). Your loan eligibility also depends on income — most banks limit the EMI to 40–50% of your net monthly income. Use our EMI calculator to find a loan amount where the EMI stays within 40% of your monthly take-home pay.
source_title: Home Loan EMI Calculator India 2026

q: Is a home loan balance transfer worth it in 2026?
a: It depends on three things: the rate gap, your outstanding balance and your remaining tenure. As a rule of thumb a balance transfer is clearly worth it when the rate gap is 50 basis points (0.50 percentage points) or more, the outstanding balance is at least Rs 15-20 lakh, and at least 7-8 years of tenure remain. Below this threshold, the switching costs (processing fee, valuation, legal, fresh stamp duty in some states) start eating most of the savings. After RBI cut the repo rate to 5.25% in December 2025, many borrowers with older loans at 8.75-9.50% are now eligible for new disbursements at 7.10-7.75% with strong-credit lenders, making early-tenure transfers more attractive than at any point in the last five years. Use this calculator to run your exact numbers.
source_title: Home Loan Balance Transfer — Is Switching Worth It?

q: What costs are involved in transferring a home loan?
a: The new lender's processing fee is the largest cost, typically 0.25-0.50% of the loan amount plus 18% GST, capped at around Rs 25,000-50,000 with most banks. Foreclosure penalty on the old loan: zero for floating-rate home loans for individual borrowers per RBI rules (effective since 2014). Fixed-rate loans may carry a 2-3% prepayment penalty - check your loan agreement before assuming. Other costs: property valuation by the new lender (Rs 3,000-5,000), title investigation report and legal fee (Rs 3,000-7,000), CERSAI search and re-registration (Rs 500-2,000), and fresh stamp duty on the new mortgage deed in some states (Maharashtra, Karnataka charge it; Delhi, Tamil Nadu typically don't on transfer; check locally). Add it all up - the all-in switching cost is usually Rs 25,000-75,000 for a Rs 50 lakh loan.
source_title: Home Loan Balance Transfer — Is Switching Worth It?

q: How long does a home loan balance transfer take?
a: Plan for 30-45 days end to end for a standard transfer. Day 1-7: apply to the new lender, submit KYC, income proofs, current bank loan statement, sanction letter and property documents. Day 7-15: new lender's credit appraisal, property valuation, legal vetting of title documents. Day 15-25: sanction letter from new lender, you accept terms, sign the new loan agreement. Day 25-35: new lender disburses directly to the old lender to close the existing loan; you receive a no-dues certificate and original property documents from the old lender (usually within 15 days of the payoff per RBI guidelines). Day 35-45: register the new mortgage with the new lender, complete CERSAI re-registration. Through this period you continue to pay EMI to the old lender.

q: Will a balance transfer hurt my CIBIL score?
a: A balance transfer involves the new lender making a hard inquiry on your credit report, which can dip your CIBIL score by 5-10 points temporarily. The closure of the old loan account is reported as 'closed' (not as default), which is neutral or mildly negative for a few months because the age of the credit relationship resets. The new account starts fresh. Net impact in 6-12 months: usually neutral to slightly positive, especially if the new EMI is more manageable and you don't miss any payment during the transition. The biggest CIBIL risk in a balance transfer is missing an EMI to the old lender during the 30-45 day transition - the new lender is not yet liable, and the old lender will report a missed payment. Set up an auto-debit reminder for the transition month.
source_title: Home Loan Balance Transfer — Is Switching Worth It?

q: Can I negotiate a rate reduction with my current lender instead?
a: Yes, and this is the cheapest first move - try it before initiating a transfer. Most Indian banks will reduce your existing rate by 25-50 basis points if you ask, especially if you have a clean repayment track record and a competitive written offer from another lender. The process is called 'rate reset' or 'spread reduction' - your existing lender adjusts the spread over the repo or external benchmark on your loan. Some banks charge a one-time conversion fee of 0.25-0.5% of the outstanding balance plus 18% GST, which is meaningfully cheaper than a full balance transfer. If the gap between your bank's reduced offer and the external offer is less than 50 basis points after accounting for the conversion fee, stay where you are. If the gap is wider, transfer.

q: How is home loan eligibility calculated in India?
a: Indian banks use the FOIR (Fixed Obligation to Income Ratio) formula: max EMI = (Net Monthly Income – Existing EMIs) × FOIR%. The FOIR limit varies by income — typically 50% for incomes below ₹50K/month, 55–60% for ₹50K–1L/month, and up to 65% for high-income earners. The maximum loan amount is then derived from this max EMI using the loan rate and tenure.
source_title: Home Loan Eligibility Calculator — Real FOIR Formula

q: What is FOIR and why does it matter?
a: FOIR (Fixed Obligation to Income Ratio) is the percentage of your monthly income that banks allow to go toward all loan EMIs combined — including the proposed home loan. SBI typically caps FOIR at 50–65% depending on income; HDFC and ICICI use similar bands. If you have a car loan, personal loan, or credit card EMI, those reduce your remaining FOIR available for the home loan.
source_title: Home Loan Eligibility Calculator — Real FOIR Formula

q: Does my co-applicant's salary increase my eligibility?
a: Yes, when you add a working co-applicant (typically spouse), their income is added to yours for FOIR calculation, often increasing eligibility by 60–90%. Both incomes must be documented (salary slips, ITR). Co-applicants can also lower interest rates in some banks if she is female (women borrowers get a 0.05–0.10% rate concession at most lenders).
source_title: Home Loan Eligibility Calculator — Real FOIR Formula

q: What is the maximum tenure for a home loan in India?
a: Most Indian banks offer maximum 30-year home loan tenure for salaried borrowers, but with an age cap — the loan must be fully paid off before retirement age (60 for most banks, 65 for select). So a 35-year-old can typically get 25 years; a 50-year-old gets 10 years. Longer tenure means lower EMI and higher eligibility, but more total interest paid.
source_title: Home Loan Eligibility Calculator — Real FOIR Formula

q: Why do different banks show different eligibility for the same income?
a: Three reasons: (1) FOIR varies — SBI is conservative at 50–55%, HDFC up to 65% for high earners. (2) Income weights — some banks discount variable pay (bonus, incentives) to 50%. (3) Co-applicant rules — some banks count 100% of co-applicant income, others only 50% if the co-applicant is unemployed but has assets. Always get pre-approval from at least 3 banks before finalising.

q: How much area to paint in a 2BHK?
a: For a typical 2BHK (carpet area 700–900 sqft), the wall surface area to paint is roughly 3× the carpet area = 2,100–2,700 sqft. This includes ceilings (1× carpet area), walls (2× carpet area), and minor structures. For a 1BHK (450–600 sqft), expect 1,400–1,800 sqft of paintable surface.

q: Should I include wall putty cost separately?
a: Yes, putty is always a separate line item from paint. Wall putty (Birla White / JK White / Asian Paints TruCare) costs ₹10–16/sqft. It's recommended for fresh new walls and any wall with hairline cracks. For repainting smooth, well-maintained walls, you can skip putty and apply primer directly. q: What is the difference between 1-coat and 2-coat painting?
a: 2-coat application is the industry standard in India and what every paint manufacturer's warranty assumes. Single-coat looks visibly streaky and uneven, especially on darker shades or rough walls. The labour difference between 1-coat and 2-coat is ~₹3–5/sqft; the paint quantity needed roughly doubles. Always insist on 2-coat in your contractor agreement — it's a common short-cut.

The premium tier difference is real; the basic tier difference is mostly marketing.
